1_dedicated_transfer.what: a ring-A-class 1.6 m spine port and 1.9 m chamber on ring B; casualties ride ring A's measured chain
1_dedicated_transfer.human_sweep_note: ring A as built is the only measured 1.6 m chain (single-seed built_A, not the worst-case method): it FAILs while spinning, so concept 1 also needs concept 3's stop
1_dedicated_transfer.refuge: through the trunk to the storm refuge (ring A's chain PASS in 0 g, MARGINAL stopped)
1_dedicated_transfer.pressure: port closures 161 kN each way against 51 kN today (CALC-R02 diagnostic)
1_dedicated_transfer.mass: a longer drum and larger closures (not estimated: no closure or drum mass is sourced)
1_dedicated_transfer.ring_stop: needed for transport (ring A pattern: FAIL spinning)
1_dedicated_transfer.reversibility: IRREVERSIBLE: the vestibule reaches 0.70 m into hub 1's forward cartridge withdrawal path; hub 1's service direction, ring B's station or in-situ cartridge service must change (rotor interface, owner architecture)
1_dedicated_transfer.story: a hospital lock between the rings

2_distributed_care_refuge_in_place.what: care at an in-sector care point (bunk, medical couch, aft burn couch; in the garden sectors a fold-down couch where Garden_Rack_1 and Mess stand); a casualty who cannot be moved shelters in the sector, the others go to the storm refuge
2_distributed_care_refuge_in_place.refuge: in place: 25.1 g/cm2 if each ring's 80 t of water sits on its three sector shells, 3.3 g/cm2 if it is spread round the whole frame (storm refuge 20); a casualty shelter at the refuge's density takes 4.1 t, redistributed
2_distributed_care_refuge_in_place.pressure: no new closure; the sector hatch stays the boundary
2_distributed_care_refuge_in_place.mass: net zero if the shelter water is redistributed from the 160 t rotating allowance (placement WORKING)
2_distributed_care_refuge_in_place.reversibility: REVERSIBLE: furniture, a garden fit-out swap and water placement; no pressure boundary, port or rotor change
2_distributed_care_refuge_in_place.story: care comes to the casualty: the sector is where the crew lives and heals

3_stopped_indexed_ring_b.what: stop both rings (one ring alone leaves its momentum on the ship), index ring B and carry the casualty through today's 0.9 m port
3_stopped_indexed_ring_b.human_sweep_note: stopping does not change the port: ring B stays FAIL (best G1 -0.135 m to the trunk)
3_stopped_indexed_ring_b.ring_stop: both rings, 1800 s down and up each (one ring stopped = 1000 x the allowed residual momentum); the whole ship at 0 g; re-index at 1.5 g NOT ALLOWED (CALC-R05)
3_stopped_indexed_ring_b.reversibility: an operating mode, not an architecture; it closes no geometry on ring B
3_stopped_indexed_ring_b.story: the ship stops for one person

why: the only concept that passes care in every ring B sector-state with reversible changes

recommendation.keeps: the care and refuge requirements; no hull cutout; ring A's chain unchanged
